question: Let $f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 12x - 5$. Show that $f(x)$ has no local maxima or minima.
explanation:
$f'(x)=3x^2-12x+12=3(x-2)^2$.

Derivative does not change sign around $x=2$.

Hence no local maximum or minimum.

options.A: $f(x)$ has a local maximum at $x=2$ because $f'(2)=0$.
options.B: $f'(x)=3(x-2)^2$ does not change sign around $x=2$, so $f(x)$ has no local maxima or minima.
options.C: $f(x)$ has a local minimum at $x=2$ because $f'(x)\ge0$.
options.D: $f(x)$ has both a local maximum and a local minimum because it is a cubic function.
